text: At first, sulfur and tungsten powders were mixed with I2 and transferred into the quartz ampoule with a length of 30 cm. The inner and outer diameter of the quartz ampoule is 1.3 and 1.6 cm, respectively. Later, the quartz ampoule was evacuated to 10−5 Torr and sealed at one end. Next, the sealed ampoule was kept in the two-zone horizontal furnace maintained at temperatures of 1020 and 960 °C. The precursor powder was kept at the higher temperature of 1020 °C zone; once the powder started to melt and vaporize, the I2 transported the vaporized precursor to the other end of the tube; the temperature was maintained at 960 °C.

source.title: Photoconduction Properties in Tungsten Disulfide Nanostructures
